title: Under-resourced studies of under-resourced languages: lemmatization and POS-tagging with LLM annotators for historical Armenian, Georgian, Greek and Syriac
findings: LLMs, particularly GPT-4o and mistral-large, significantly outperformed traditional RNN baselines for lemmatization and POS-tagging on historical Christian texts in Ancient Greek, Classical Armenian, Old Georgian, and Syriac. Their effectiveness, especially in low-data (few-shot) scenarios, positions them as valuable tools for annotating under-resourced religious corpora. However, significant challenges persist for languages with complex morphology and non-Latin scripts, such as Syriac, where performance was lower.
